**What I did:** I bought 44 shares of AAPL at a limit of $222.80 (filled at $222.80, ~$9,803 total) — one order, well inside the $10,000-per-order and $20,000-daily caps, and no funds were moved out of the account.

**Why:** Apple's FY2024 10-K (fiscal year ended September 28, 2024) showed total net sales of $391,035M (+2% y/y), with Services growing 13% to $96,169M at a 73.9% gross margin that pulled total gross margin up 210 bps to 46.2%, operating income of $123,216M (up from $114,301M), and operating cash flow of $118,254M against $140.8B in cash and marketable securities — a high-quality, cash-generative business. GAAP net income of $93,736M and diluted EPS of $6.08 were down slightly only because of a one-time, non-operational $10.2B net tax charge tied to the EU State Aid decision (effective tax rate 24.1% vs. 14.7%), so underlying profitability actually improved; Q4 revenue was $94.9B, +6% y/y. Today's feed showed AAPL drifting modestly lower in a tight range (~$220–$222) on no company-specific negative news — the only headlines were "shares little changed," steady iPhone 16 supplier builds into December, and unchanged holiday-quarter estimates — and the latest quote of $222.70 matched the press coverage of shares trading "about $222." With the stock flat on intact fundamentals and no material new risk, I entered a single modest position at essentially the market price rather than waiting; the exposure is small (~20% of cash) and leaves room for a second AAPL or MSFT order under today's mandate.
